$comment: Board3's real design rules. This file exists because KiCad's EasyEDA Pro
importer does NOT translate design rules -- it brings geometry, nets and the
schematic faithfully, then writes KiCad's stock factory defaults into the
That substitution is silent and expensive. Measured against those invented
rules, an untouched Board3 reports 544 DRC violations, 503 of them clearance
-- every one a false positive, all sitting in a 0.117-0.197 mm band just under
a 0.2 mm rule the board was never drawn to. Against the real rules below the

same board reported 41 at import time -- EasyEDA's own DRC was right all along. Those 41 have since been cleared and Board3 measures 0; both CI gates are absolute at zero, so 41 is history, not a floor.
Anyone migrating a board here who trusts the imported .kicad_pro will chase
hundreds of phantom violations and route to constraints their fab never agreed

$notes.track_width: 0.254 mm (10 mil) is what every track on Board3 actually is, so it is the design's working width rather than the process floor. The 0.1016 mm minimum is JLC's standard limit; 0.09 mm (3.5 mil) is reachable on their ADVANCED process at extra cost, which is what an autorouter necks down to at fine-pitch pads if it is not constrained.
$notes.annular_ring: JLC wants 0.15 mm minimum, 0.2 mm preferred (re-verified against jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities on 2026-07-27: 'recommended 0.20 mm or above; absolute minimum 0.15 mm' for multilayer 1oz). It IS expressible -- min_via_annular_width, added above on 2026-07-27. Leaving it out cost real money in attention: the importer's .kicad_pro carries 0.1, so for four units every DRC run in this plan measured annular rings against a rule the board was never designed to, and a 0.5/0.3 via with a 0.10 mm ring that U5 introduced went unreported until kicad-happy's DFM check found it. A rule you do not encode is a rule you are not checking. UPDATED 2026-07-31: the whole via population was moved from 0.6/0.3 (ring 0.150, exactly JLC absolute minimum, zero registration margin) to 0.6/0.25 (ring 0.175). COUNT CORRECTED 2026-08-03: this note used to name a fixed population of '198 vias'. That was wrong when written, and a hardcoded count rots on every routing change anyway -- measured 222 on 2026-08-03 (221 at 0.6/0.25 plus the single 0.5/0.2 at U1.93). Do not cite a via count from this file; count them, by iterating PCB_VIA_T over board.Tracks(). The obvious move -- growing the via to 0.7/0.35 -- was tried first and produced 535 DRC violations (514 clearance, 20 hole-to-hole), because this board is routed tight against 0.6 mm copper; it would need a full re-route. Shrinking the DRILL buys the identical ring with zero copper growth and zero new violations. Cost consequence recorded below.
$notes.min_hole_size: min_through_hole_diameter is 0.3 mm here as a COST floor, not a capability floor -- JLC's published range is 0.15-6.3 mm. CORRECTED 2026-08-03: this note used to say drills under 0.3 mm 'can attract a surcharge', and that model is wrong. JLC conditions the via surcharge on via DIAMETER below 0.45 mm, not on drill size. Board3's vias are 0.60 and 0.50 mm in diameter, so NO surcharge applies to any of them at any drill this board uses. Keeping the floor is still reasonable as a conservative default for new holes, but it must not be cited as a price argument -- the wrong model already drove a real design decision (it is why the 0.7/0.35 option was weighed against a cost that did not exist). One deliberate exception exists on Board3: the BTN1 via at U1.93 is 0.5/0.2 because its pad neighbours cap the diameter at 0.517 mm and the ring rule has to win.
$notes.hole_clearance: 0.2 mm matches JLC's published via-hole-to-track limit and mirrors the value d74143a set in the board's own .kicad_pro on 2026-08-02. It sat at 0.1016 here for three days after that commit -- the same figure as min_clearance and min_track_width, which is almost certainly where it was copied from -- and because _rules_project() overwrites the staged project with this file, the CI gate was judging hole clearance at half the fab's limit. A rule raised on the board is not raised until it is raised HERE. JLC publishes TWO limits that KiCad's single min_hole_clearance cannot express: via-to-track 0.2 and PTH-to-track 0.28 (0.35 recommended). This key carries the via figure because it is the binding one for the tightest hole on the board (0.2730 via->track); the stricter PTH case is enforced separately by the pth_hole_to_track_jlc rule in the board's .kicad_dru. Measured 2026-08-05: tightest via 0.2730, tightest PTH 0.4547, tightest NPTH 0.3377, and zero PTH pads in the 0.20-0.28 band.

differential_pairs.$resolved: 2026-07-27. Resolved by MEASUREMENT of the board rather than recovery from EasyEDA, because the measurement made recovery moot: ALL 2435 tracks on Board3 are 0.254 mm. There is exactly one track width on this board and no differential-pair geometry was ever applied in copper. Whatever the EasyEDA net-class panel said, it did not shape this board -- so these are decisions to make, not values to recover. The '10mm' memory is 10 mil = 0.254 mm, i.e. the board-wide default, which is consistent with no pair-specific rule having reached copper.
differential_pairs.$stackup_assumption: The importer carried NO stackup block, so impedance is computed against JLCPCB's standard 4-layer 1.6 mm stackup (JLC04161H-7628): Top 1oz / prepreg 7628 0.2104 mm Er~4.4 / Inner1 / core 1.065 mm / Inner2 / prepreg 0.2104 mm / Bottom 1oz. Figures below are closed-form edge-coupled microstrip for a top-layer pair over a SOLID Inner1 ground. CONFIRM against JLCPCB's own impedance calculator before fabrication, and confirm the reference plane is actually continuous under each pair -- an impedance number over a split plane is fiction.
differential_pairs.$as_drawn: 0.254 mm trace over 0.2104 mm prepreg gives Zo ~60 ohm single-ended. At the board's 0.254 mm spacing that is Zdiff ~102 ohm -- inside USB's 90 ohm +/-15% window (76.5-103.5) but sitting at its top edge, and low for CAN's 120 ohm.

USB.note: Keep the board-wide 0.254 mm width and TIGHTEN THE GAP to 0.15 mm. This is the minimal-change option: it preserves the single-width virtue of the board, and it matches the lost action item's wording -- 'narrow it' meant narrow the gap, not the trace. Narrowing the TRACE would raise impedance away from 90 ohm, which is the trap in that note. Alternative if a 0.15 mm gap is uncomfortable: 0.30 mm width with 0.21 mm gap, also ~90 ohm.

CAN_retired.$retired: 2026-08-01. The 120 ohm target is RETIRED, not met. It was never reached in copper: CAN2's tightest approach is ~0.406 mm centre-to-centre (~0.15 mm edge gap) -- USB's tight-coupling geometry, the opposite of what CAN wants -- and CAN1's legs run uncoupled for most of their length. So the two pairs missed the same target in opposite directions.
CAN_retired.$why_retired: At 1 Mbps a 5 m stub-free segment is electrically short; reflection amplitude is bounded by the mismatch and the bus is terminated at its ends by the vehicle harness (J3/J4 stay OPEN by design). The repo's own analysis already argued coupling is not load-bearing here. Opening CAN2's gap to >=0.5 mm means re-routing a pair on an otherwise-clean board to chase a number nothing measures.
CAN_retired.$if_this_changes: Reinstate if the bus ever runs faster than 1 Mbps, leaves the vehicle harness, or grows stubs. The original target is preserved below.

$original_target.computed_zdiff_ohm: 114 at 0.5 mm gap, 118 at 0.75 mm gap
$original_target.note: CAN wants the OPPOSITE treatment to USB: loosely coupled. With 0.254 mm traces, Zdiff asymptotically approaches 2*Zo = ~120 ohm as the gap grows, so a WIDE gap (>=0.5 mm) is what reaches 120 ohm. Tightening a CAN pair the way you tighten USB drives it away from target. In practice this matters little at 1 Mbps over 23-25 mm of track -- symmetry, equal via counts and the split termination dominate -- so treat the gap as a target, not a constraint to contort the layout around.

cost_floors_mm.$comment: Not capability limits -- price breaks. DRC must not fail on these or the gate stops meaning anything, so tools/kicad_verify.py reports them as an advisory line instead. Anything listed here needs a recorded reason, the way U1.93's 0.2 mm drill has one. EXCEPTION 2026-07-31: the whole via population now drills 0.25 mm, under this 0.3 mm floor. Reason: it is the only way to get annular-ring margin on an already-routed board (see annular_ring note). JLC capability min is 0.15 mm so this is buildable. RESOLVED 2026-08-03: the earlier instruction to 'confirm the surcharge at quote time' is withdrawn -- there is no surcharge to confirm. JLC gates it on via diameter below 0.45 mm and every via here is 0.60 or 0.50, so the drill size costs nothing. See the min_hole_size note.
